_comment: MEASUREMENTS, not settings. Regenerated by scripts/deploy_calibrate.py -- do not hand-edit.
Same split configs/vision.yaml documents: numbers you argue about live in a yaml config,
outputs of a calibration script live here.
EVERY COORDINATE HERE IS IN DEVICE PIXELS -- the Android screen's own 1920x1080, which is
what `adb sendevent` addresses. It is fixed by the emulator and has nothing to do with the
monitor's resolution or with what mss grabs. Tap targets and the joystick anchor are used
in this space directly.
The GATE reads the same buttons out of a captured frame instead, and that frame is at the
vision stack's calibrated 2002x1126 viewport, not at 1080p. Calibration.viewport_button()
does the conversion; nothing here needs restating in viewport pixels. See capture.py for
why the resize targets 2002x1126 and BRAWL_DEPLOYMENT_DESIGN.md 9.3 for the decision.
Buttons MEASURED from a temporal median of tests/fixtures/vision/bluestacks-example-new.mp4
via HoughCircles + gameplay.ring_score_at refinement. Note this needed minRadius=20: the
shipped gameplay.RADIUS_PX = (40, 115) never proposes these buttons, which is why
calibrate_buttons returns zero anchors on this footage.
Joystick MEASURED live by injecting held contacts in a training ground -- see its notes.
RE-LABELLED 2026-09-22: every name under `buttons` was on the wrong disc, rotated by one.
No coordinate moved. See that block's notes for how it happened and how it was confirmed.
MEASURED by scripts/deploy_calibrate.py against the LIVE mss capture, from a temporal
median of 31 gameplay frames at the deployment viewport, then
converted back to device pixels. This is the source the match gate actually reads, which
the previous fit (an OBS recording's median) was not -- see BRAWL_DEPLOYMENT_DESIGN.md
4.5 on radii not transferring between frame sources.
CENTRES are authoritative. RADII are still advisory: MatchState.refine() re-fits the
gate anchor's radius on the first gameplay frame of every run, and that stays true even
when the stored radius came from the same kind of source.
Refitted 2026-09-09, recorded here under the PRE-ROTATION names: `attack` score 0.960
shift 2.6px, `gadget` 0.753 / 0.8px, `super` 0.987 / 2.7px. Read those as today's
gadget, Super and hypercharge, in that order.
NAMES RE-LABELLED BY HAND on 2026-09-22, and NOT ONE COORDINATE CHANGED. All three sat
on the wrong disc, rotated by one: what this file called `attack` is the GADGET, what it
called `gadget` is the SUPER, and what it called `super` is the HYPERCHARGE. The operator
identified all three off a live frame -- the gadget is the bright green disc at the
bottom right of the arc carrying a shovel, the Super is the blue skull above and left of
it, and the third is the hypercharge, which Mortis does not have.
Every score, radius and margin measured before that date is still valid. They were honest
measurements of these discs under the wrong names, which is why the fix is a rename and
why re-fitting would have found nothing.
NOTHING HERE COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, and that is worth stating once:
fit_buttons() is a REFINER. It searches near each stored centre, so it confirms that a
disc is there and can never notice that it is the wrong disc. Its own docstring warns
against guessing names from geometry; the seed names were simply never verified.
the `tap` job proves the attack fires by watching ammo drop, but an attack press reads
control.attack_tap out of configs/deployment.yaml and never this table.
the `super` job taps this table and WOULD have caught it, but it reports `skipped`
rather than failing when the Super is not charged, so a wrong point and an uncharged
Super produce the same output.
the gadget was not pressed by anything until SIM_OVERHAUL Step G5, on 2026-09-21.
A name here is an IDENTIFICATION and no script in this repo can produce one. That is the
one thing in this file that is hand-set, and the reason the `_comment` says otherwise for
everything else.
`hypercharge` is CONFIRMED by the operator, 2026-09-22: it is the hypercharge button.
Mortis has no hypercharge, so it is drawn but INERT -- it never fills, never sweeps and
never animates. That is a stronger property than 'nothing presses it', which is all the
gate was originally chosen on, and it is why the gate sits here.
THAT SAFETY IS CONDITIONAL ON THE ROSTER. Give Mortis a hypercharge and this disc gains a
charge meter that fills during a match, which is exactly what disqualifies the Super: the
Super's in-match ring floor is 0.675 on the fixture clip because its face changes as it
charges, and that cost two weeks of a failing test. Re-measure this gate if the brawler or
its unlocks change.
THERE IS NO `attack` ENTRY, deliberately. Attack is an AREA, not a button: any tap on the
right of the screen fires, control.attack_tap picks a clearance point for it, and the
stick FLOATS to wherever it is touched rather than living at a fixed centre. The stick's
rest circle is real, at about (1745.9, 829.2, 45.4), but it moves whenever the agent
attacks, scores only 0.718 on a live median, and never opens the gate on the fixture clip.
Which button anchor gates 'are we in a match'. `hypercharge`: the hypercharge button,
which Mortis does not have, so nothing presses it and nothing charges it either. See the
roster caveat under `buttons` for when that stops being true.
MOVED 2026-09-22, with the re-labelling above. The anchor was the disc this file called
`gadget`, which is really the SUPER. The old rationale ('the one button the policy never
presses') was therefore false for every super press, and a fired Super greys its button
for the whole recharge -- far longer than the 4-tick exit. SIM_OVERHAUL Step G6 asked
whether a gadget tap could break this gate; the real answer is that the gate was never on
the gadget.

CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-09-22 in a real match, runs/audit/gadget_anchor_trace.json: 264 ticks
at 12 Hz, one gadget tap at tick 24, controls up throughout. `hypercharge` held at 0.991
CAVEAT on that trace: `hypercharge` and `super` are BIT-IDENTICAL across all 264 ticks,
one distinct score and one distinct colour each, equal to their own refine scores, while
the tapped gadget varied across 111 scores. Either a lossless capture of a static region
or a stale ROI for the non-tapped anchors; the frames are gone, so it is not decidable.
The anchor rests on the bakeoff and on the disc being inert, not on this. See STEPS G6.2.
with a floor of 0.991, zero ticks under threshold, zero exits and zero colour movement
across the whole 22 s. `super` held flat at 0.766. The 2-of-3 vote held throughout.
The same trace shows the hazard G6 was written about is REAL, on the disc this file had
mislabelled: the gadget's colour moved 224.3 levels, its shadow gate FALSE-EXITED at
t=+0.58 s, and it stayed under 0.45 for 60 consecutive ticks -- 5.0 s -- bottoming out
at 0.164 at t=+18.4 s as the recharge sweep completed. An agent gated on its own gadget
would have stopped dead for five seconds after every throw. The earlier probe could not
have found this: it tapped the Super and watched the Super.
match_gate._samples_comment: DURATIONS, expressed in perception ticks: 0.5 s to enter and 0.33 s to exit. They were 10 and 6, which were those same durations at 20 Hz; loop.tick_hz is now 12 (design 6.13) so the counts move with it. Asymmetric on purpose -- entering wrongly sprays input at a menu, exiting wrongly stands still for a beat -- and exit cannot be instant because a Super detonating over the button drops the score for a few mid-match frames.

_comment: MEASURED live, by injecting held contacts in the training ground and reading the knob's
own position back off the framebuffer.
The stick SATURATES AT 92 px. Commanding 140 px produced a 91.7 / 92.6 / 92.0 px knob
deflection across three directions -- the game clamps, so anything past ~92 is full speed
and the exact value stops mattering. radius_px is set to 110: 20% past saturation so a
small anchor or UI-scale drift cannot fall short of full speed, and tight enough that the
reachable circle stays clear of the bottom UI strip.
Directions verified against the sim's own bins at the same time: bin 0 -> (+91.7, -0.1)
(right), bin 8 -> (-92.6, -1.6) (left), bin 2 -> (+64.4, +65.6) (45 deg DOWN-right, which
is the no-y-flip convention confirmed empirically). Idle returned the knob to within 1.1 px
of the anchor WITHOUT releasing the contact.
anchor is the design's proposed (0.18*W, 0.62*H): centre-left, clearance greater than the
saturation radius in all four directions. Deliberately NOT the bottom-left rest position,
which has no clearance down or left. It worked unmodified.
